text.p: Bonds closed well-supported along the curve, with the longer end capable of narrowing the spread with the German Bunds, traders said.

They said the spread between the 10-year cash bonds could dip towards 75 basis points against its close at 81 basis points on Monday. "If Spain (spread vs Bund) goes to 85 basis points, Portugal could reach 75", said one fixed-income trader.

Support at the short to medium end was more than confirmed by declining rates in the Forward Rate Adjustment (FRA) and swap markets, they said. Tomorrow's three-year bond auction was likely to draw strong support, they added.

Traders said the market had been galvanised by Brussels' approval of the Portuguese and Spanish economic convergence plans. "There is great confidence in our convergence for the single currency and the (10-year) spreads can fall," said the fixed-income trader.
Traders said that the only factor that could hold the market back would be a weaker escudo, although they noted this was due to the softer dollar rather than internal considerations.
Three-year swap rates closed between 5.51 and 5.56 percent against 5.54 and 5.60 percent at the opening.
